title: The largest schematic open of an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology] and open subspaces [def-a1-space-open-subspace, def-weil-open-immersion]. There is an open subspace $X_{\mathrm{sch}}\subseteq X$ represented by an $S$-scheme which contains every open subspace of $X$ represented by an $S$-scheme. Its point set is the union of the point sets of all such open subspaces. No separation or quasi-compactness hypothesis is assumed; this open may be empty.

proof.text: By [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], open subspaces of $X$ correspond bijectively, preserving inclusion, to open subsets of the set $|X|$. Thus their isomorphism classes form a set. Let $I$ index precisely those open subspaces $X_i$ represented by $S$-schemes. Each $|X_i|$ is open, so $O=\bigcup_{i\in I}|X_i|$ is open. The same correspondence gives an open subspace $J\subseteq X$ with point image $O$.

For each $i$, $|X_i|\subseteq O$, so [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests] gives a unique factorization $X_i\to J\to X$. Regard $X_i$ as a subfunctor of $J$; sectionwise injectivity follows from its inclusion in $X$. For every $S$-scheme $T\to J$, the same node identifies $X_i\times_JT$ with $X_i\times_XT$. The latter is an open subscheme of $T$ by [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. Hence every $X_i\to J$ is representable by open immersions.

For a scheme $T$ and a section $a\in J(T)$, let $T_i\subseteq T$ represent $h_T\times_JX_i$. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], its point image in $T$ is $|a|^{-1}(|X_i|)$, viewing $|X_i|$ inside $|J|$. These opens cover $T$: for each $t\in T$, $|a|(t)\in |J|=O$, hence lies in some $|X_i|$. The projection to $X_i$ says exactly that $a|_{T_i}\in X_i(T_i)$. Thus the subfunctors $X_i$ cover $J$ in the sense of [def-pc-cover].

The open subspace $J$ is an algebraic space by [def-a1-space-open-subspace], hence an fppf sheaf by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Every Zariski open covering is an fppf covering by [lem-pc-zariski-coverings-are-fppf]. The sheaf equalizer condition of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], applied to this covering, therefore gives unique gluing of matching sections of $J$ on Zariski opens. This is precisely [def-pc-zariski-sheaf-property].

Apply [lem-pc-schemes-criterion] to $F=J$ and the set-indexed subfunctors $(X_i)_{i\in I}$. Step 4 supplies its Zariski sheaf condition; each $X_i$ is represented by an $S$-scheme by the definition of $I$; step 2 supplies open representability of each inclusion; step 3 supplies the cover. Consequently $J$ is represented by an $S$-scheme.

source.place: Tag 01JJ, lemma-glue-functors; applied as in Tag 03JH, lemma-subscheme.

proof.text: Set $X_{\mathrm{sch}}=J$. Every schematic open subspace of $X$ is one of the $X_i$, and step 2 already provides its inclusion in $J$. Thus $J$ contains every schematic open and has exactly their union as point set, by step 1. The construction uses neither separation nor quasi-compactness. No step requires $O$ to be nonempty: when $O=\varnothing$, every test scheme admitting a section of $J$ is empty, the covering condition still holds, and the same criterion applies.
